summary: Guidance requested: post-optimization latency spike after enabling batching, caching, and quantization; need safe rollback plan
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a ~2-3x increase in median token latency after applying Optimize recommendations (continuous batching, prefix caching, and int8 quantization profile) to a dedicated pool.
Impact: Production traffic for Acme Health Analytics experiences elevated latency for generate/chat endpoints; rate of client timeouts increased from ~0.5% to ~7% over 24h window.
Environment: Dedicated cluster for Acme (us-east-1), model pinned to gpt-redwood-1.3b-quantized-int8, autoscaling enabled, recently updated config via Redwood Console Optimize suggestion.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send standard chat completion (system+user) 2) Observe request latency distribution in Console -> Routes 3) Compare before/after change window.
Expected behavior: 10-20% token-level CPU/GPU improvement with similar or improved latency.
Actual behavior: Median token latency increased, tail latency spiked, and several streaming connections dropped mid-response.
Request IDs / sample logs: req-20260310-4f1a7 (high tail latency), req-20260311-b8c2d (stream disconnect).
steps_to_reproduce: Apply Optimize recommendations (enable continuous batching, enable prefix/KV caching TTL=900s, apply int8 quantization profile) to dedicated pool
Run 1k chat generation requests at production qps
Monitor per-token latency and streaming disconnects in Console > Routes > Live traces

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Quantization profile introduced numerical instability for certain attention patterns -> increased compute per token due to fallback or additional kernels.
Hypothesis B: Batching coalescing increased tail latency under our request size distribution; inter-request variance causing batch queuing delays.
Hypothesis C: Prefix/KV cache misconfiguration (TTL too long / cache key mismatch) causing cache churn and ineffective reuse.
Ran quick A/B: rolled optimization config to canary (10% traffic) and observed canary median stayed baseline but 100% rollout showed spike -> suggests interaction at full load.
Checked kernel metrics and saw increase in 'kernel_fallback' counter on nodes running quantized model (link: Console -> Nodes -> Node-12 metrics).
No related infra events or GPU OOMs in cluster logs.

2026-03-10 Jordan Liu (SRE): Noted kernel_fallback counts increasing; requested customer to pin previous non-quantized model for baseline comparison.

2026-03-11 Acme Support Contact (Laura Chen): Confirmed they applied Optimize recommendations yesterday and attached sample traces (see logs above); asked for rollback plan that minimizes request loss.
2026-03-11 Jordan Liu (SRE): Performed canary rollback on 10% traffic; canary metrics look stable. Preparing safe rollback runbook for full revert.
resolution:
Workaround: Advised customer to revert to previous model variant (gpt-redwood-1.3b) and disable continuous batching while we investigate quantization kernel fallback. Steps taken: 1) Pinned model version to gpt-redwood-1.3b via Console (route pin applied at 2026-03-11T09:15Z). 2) Rolled back prefix cache TTL change to previous 300s. 3) Reduced batch_max_tokens to 512 and set batching window to 20ms.
Full rollback plan (safe): - Create canary route at 5% traffic to pinned non-quantized model and observe for 30m. - Drain connections from quantized variant using traffic shift policy (30% -> 5% over 10m), then remove variant. - Revert quantization profile in Optimize to previous profile and disable in cluster config. - Monitor Console dashboards (median token latency, streaming disconnects, kernel_fallback) and keep on-call SRE loop. - If rollback is successful, coordinate with applied Optimize PR revert (related_github_prs above) and schedule a postmortem.
Follow-up: Engineering to reproduce perf regression in staging with same request distribution; Research to validate quantization kernels. Customer monitoring link + runbook shared. Status: In Progress; awaiting Engineering validation before marking Resolved.
